messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Families can bring items to the library desk between 8:15 and 3:30 on school days. The main entrance opens at 8:00, but the library desk is not staffed before 8:15. Equipment should be returned by the student or an adult listed as an authorized contact. The school has not asked students to leave devices unattended outside the library.

The loan pool includes Chromebooks, padded sleeves, power adapters, and a small number of wireless mice. Each item has a Cedar Grove inventory sticker, usually on the underside or inside flap. The Chromebook number is also printed on its login card. Some families received a sleeve and adapter together, while others received only a Chromebook. A mouse was optional, not part of every loan. The family’s issue sheet, sent home in September, lists the items assigned to that student; the office can look up the list if the sheet is missing. Students should not write their passwords on the issue sheet or put them inside the device sleeve.

At the library desk, staff will check the inventory sticker against the return log and look for the issued accessories. They will make a brief visual check for obvious damage, but the desk check is not a repair assessment. Families do not need to erase files or sign out of the school account before returning a Chromebook. Staff will handle account sign-out after intake. A cracked corner, loose hinge, or screen mark should be mentioned at the desk so it can be noted accurately; reporting damage is not, by itself, a statement about who caused it. One parent said, “I can bring the Chromebook, but I’m not sure where the little charger went.” The librarian replied, “Bring what you have, and we’ll compare it with the issue sheet.”

The return log has separate boxes for “received,” “accessory missing,” and “needs follow-up.” Staff should not mark a set complete just because the Chromebook is present. If an issued adapter or sleeve is absent at the desk, the Chromebook can still be received, but the log must show the missing accessory and staff should give the family a small yellow reminder slip listing what was not present. If the family brings the missing item later, staff can add it to that student’s log entry. The reminder slip is a record of the items still to be checked, not a fee notice or a decision about responsibility.

1. Return-day handling and alternate drop-off
   If a family brings the assigned equipment to the staffed library desk by 3:30 p.m. on Friday, May 22, staff should check the inventory and accessories there and record what is physically received. If the family cannot come during the library desk hours, they may place the equipment in a closed bag with the student’s name and grade written on the outside and take it to the main office before 4:00 p.m. on May 22. In that alternative case, office staff should give the bag to the library team for checking on the next school day; the office receipt is not confirmation that every assigned item is inside. Do not direct families to leave equipment at the entrance or put it in the library’s after-hours book slot, which is for books only.

On Tuesday morning, May 19, the library team tested the return log with two sample records and found that the accessory boxes were easy to overlook on a phone screen. They enlarged those fields and added a prompt for the staff member to read the assigned-item list before closing an entry. The team plans to use the revised log throughout the return window. The office copier is available for extra issue sheets, but staff should first check whether a family needs a replacement rather than automatically printing one. Ms. Imani Patel, the library assistant, will be at the desk each day from 8:15 to 12:30; the afternoon desk is covered by the rotating office aide. Families can ask either person where to wait, but students should keep the walkway to the circulation counter clear.

Several practical details came up during the first day of reminders. One student carried a Chromebook in a sports bag with a wet towel, so the library team asked families to keep devices dry and separate from food or drink. Another family brought an adapter with no visible inventory sticker; staff matched it to the student’s listed model but did not assume that every unmarked adapter belonged to the same loan. The return desk has a small paper tray for login cards and issue sheets, and staff can return a family’s copy after checking it. A guardian asked, “Do we need to wait while you test the whole computer?” The desk aide answered, “No, we check the sticker and the outside here; technical checks happen later.” Keep that distinction clear so a quick intake is not described as a full device test.

2. Dates, follow-up, and communication
   The school sends a reminder through its family portal on May 15 and a final reminder on May 21. The reminders should say where and when to return equipment, what to bring if available, and how the alternate office drop-off works. They should not claim that every student received every accessory. A family that cannot locate an item can still return the other assigned equipment during the window and speak with staff about the missing item. If a family needs language assistance, the office can arrange a call with the school’s interpreter service; families should contact the main office rather than write private student information in a public message thread. The general office number on the school calendar is the appropriate contact route.

If the library team finds a discrepancy after a bag has been left at the office, it should contact the listed adult using the school’s usual private communication channel and describe only the item that needs clarification. It should not tell a student in a hallway that the family owes money or has lost school property. The notes do not establish a fee, replacement charge, or consequence for any missing or damaged item, and the return guide should not imply one. The school wants accurate records and a straightforward way for families to ask questions; it has not announced a decision about individual cases. When a family later brings an item shown as missing on the reminder slip, staff should update the existing log entry rather than start a duplicate record.

After the May 22 window, the school will review the intake log and contact families only where an assigned item still needs clarification. No one should promise that a device will be available for a particular student next term, because next year’s assignments have not been made. The guide can explain that the library team will check returned equipment after intake and that families may be contacted about a recorded discrepancy. Keep the description modest: staff can confirm what was handed in and what still needs follow-up, but they should not present a visual desk check as proof that a device works. The purpose of the guide is to help families complete the return, understand the two drop-off routes, and know what to expect if an accessory is not there.
